questions.question: The amount on a sum of ₹5,000 at 20% per annum compound interest, compounded annually, in 2 years, will be:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective rate of compound interest for 2 years at 20% p.a. = 20 + 20 + (20 × 20) ÷ 100 = 44%.

Total amount = 100% (Principal) + 44% (Interest) = 144% of Principal.

Amount = 144% of 5000 = (144 ÷ 100) × 5000 = 144 × 50 = 7200.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹7,200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹5,000

Rate (R) = 20% p.a.

Time (T) = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P × (1 + R ÷ 100)T

 
 
 

 
 

 
 
• 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Year 0
 Year 1
 Year 2
 
 ₹5000
 ₹6000
 A = ?
 
 
 

 

 
 
 +20%
 +20%

**Calculations:**

⇒ A = 5000 × (1 + 20 ÷ 100)²

⇒ A = 5000 × (1 + 1 ÷ 5)²

⇒ A = 5000 × (6 ÷ 5)²

⇒ A = 5000 × (36 ÷ 25)

⇒ A = 200 × 36

⇒ A = 7200

**∴ The correct answer is ₹7,200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Rate of CI

For 2 years, the effective compound interest rate can be calculated using the formula: Rₑffₑ꜀ₜᵢvₑ = X + Y + (X × Y) ÷ 100.

Difference between CI and SI

For 2 years, the exact difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest on a principal P is given by: Difference = P × (R ÷ 100)².

Half-Yearly Compounding

When interest is compounded half-yearly, the rate of interest becomes half (R ÷ 2) and the time period is doubled (2 × T).

questions.question: Seven years ago from now, a man was five times as old as his son. Seven years from now, the father will be three times as old as his son. Find the son's present age.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use elimination by subtracting both conditions

(F+7) − (F−7) = 3(S+7) − 5(S−7)

14 = 3S + 21 − 5S + 35

14 = −2S + 56 ⇒ 2S = 42

**∴ Answer = 21 years**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Let present age of father = F and son = S

7 years ago: F − 7 = 5(S − 7)

7 years later: F + 7 = 3(S + 7)

**Formula used:**

Form linear equations and solve simultaneously

**Calculation:**

⇒ F − 7 = 5S − 35

⇒ F = 5S − 28

⇒ F + 7 = 3S + 21

⇒ F = 3S + 14

⇒ 5S − 28 = 3S + 14

⇒ 2S = 42

⇒ S = 21

**∴ The correct answer is 21.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Linear Equations

Two equations with two variables can be solved using substitution or elimination method.

Age Difference Concept

The difference between ages of two persons remains constant over time.

Verification Method

Substitute obtained value back into original equations to verify correctness.

questions.question: The mode of the observations 21, 32, 34, 34, 34, 20, 32, 24, 34, 34, 20, 25, 29, 26 and 20 is:4287
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The mode of any given data set is simply the value that appears most frequently.

By scanning the given numbers directly, we can count the occurrences of the most repeated values.

The number 34 appears exactly 5 times, which is the maximum frequency among all observations.

**∴ The correct answer is 34.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The observations are: 21, 32, 34, 34, 34, 20, 32, 24, 34, 34, 20, 25, 29, 26, 20.

**Formula Used:**

Mode = The observation with the highest frequency in the data set.

 Frequency of Observations
 Value 20 :
 
 3
 Value 32 :
 
 2
 Value 34 :
 
 5 (Max)
 Others :
 
 1 each
 
• 
 Mode = 34

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let us arrange the given data in ascending order to easily group and count the frequencies:

⇒ Data set: 20, 20, 20, 21, 24, 25, 26, 29, 32, 32, 34, 34, 34, 34, 34

⇒ Observing the arranged data, we evaluate the frequency (number of occurrences) of each value:

⇒ Frequency of 20 = 3

⇒ Frequency of 32 = 2

⇒ Frequency of 34 = 5

⇒ Frequencies of 21, 24, 25, 26, and 29 = 1 each

⇒ The mode is defined as the observation carrying the maximum frequency.

⇒ Here, the highest frequency is 5, which distinctly corresponds to the observation 34.

**∴ The correct answer is 34.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean

Mean represents the true average of all the observations in a data set. It is calculated algebraically as: Mean = Sum of all observations ÷ Total number of observations.

Median

Median identifies the exact middlemost value when data is arranged in ascending or descending order. For an odd number of observations 'n', Median = ((n + 1) ÷ 2)th term.

Empirical Relationship

For a moderately skewed statistical distribution, the mean, median, and mode are fundamentally connected by the empirical formula: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.

questions.question: Priya buys a mobile phone for her child. The phone is marked at ₹34,400 and is offered with two successive discounts of 13% and Z\% , respectively. After receiving both discounts, she pays ₹22,446. Find the value of Z .
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use successive discount multiplier concept

Final Price = MP × (1 − 13/100) × (1 − Z/100)

22446 = 34400 × 0.87 × (1 − Z/100)

22446 = 29928 × (1 − Z/100)

(1 − Z/100) = 22446 ÷ 29928 = 0.75 ⇒ Z = 25

**∴ Answer = 25%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price = 34400, First discount = 13%, Second discount = Z%

Final Price = 22446

**Formula used:**

Final Price = MP × (1 − d1/100) × (1 − d2/100)

**Calculation:**

⇒ 22446 = 34400 × (1 − 13/100) × (1 − Z/100)

⇒ 22446 = 34400 × 87/100 × (1 − Z/100)

⇒ 22446 = 29928 × (1 − Z/100)

⇒ (1 − Z/100) = 22446 ÷ 29928

⇒ (1 − Z/100) = 3 ÷ 4

⇒ Z/100 = 1 − 3/4 = 1/4

⇒ Z = 25

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discount

Net discount = a + b − (ab/100). For 13% and Z%, net discount can be computed using this formula.

Multiplier Method

Each discount converts into multiplier form: (1 − d/100). Multiply all to get final price.

Equivalent Fraction Trick

If ratio simplifies to common fraction like 3/4, it helps quickly find percentage values.

questions.question: (1)/(30) { is what percentage of } (2)/(30)?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

When the bases (denominators) of two fractions are identical, compare their numerators directly.

⇒ Required Percentage = (Numerator 1 ÷ Numerator 2) × 100

⇒ (1 ÷ 2) × 100

⇒ 50%

**∴ The correct answer is 50%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Given value = 1/30

Base value = 2/30

**Formula Used:**

Percentage = (Given Value ÷ Base Value) × 100

 
 
 1/30
 1/30
 
•

• 
 Base Value = 2/30 (100%)
 
•

• 
 Given Value = 1/30 (50%)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Percentage = (1/30) ÷ (2/30) × 100

⇒ Percentage = (1/30) × (30/2) × 100

⇒ Percentage = (1/2) × 100

⇒ Percentage = 50%

**∴ The correct answer is 50%.**

**__Additional Information__**

X is what percent of Y

It is simply the ratio of X to Y expressed out of 100. Formula: (X ÷ Y) × 100.

Percentage Change

Find the difference between new and old values, and divide by the old base value. Formula: (Difference ÷ Initial Value) × 100.

Fraction to Percentage Conversion

To convert any fraction into a percentage, directly multiply the fraction by 100. For example, 1/4 × 100 = 25%.

questions.question: Preeti, Qadir and Reena invest sum in the ratio 2 : 8 : 13, respectively. If they earned total profit of ₹87,193 at the end of year, then what is the positive difference between share of Preeti and Reena?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference depends on ratio difference only

Total ratio = 2 + 8 + 13 = 23

Difference ratio (Reena − Preeti) = 13 − 2 = 11

Difference = 87193 × (11 ÷ 23)

= 3791 × 11 = 41701

**∴ Answer = 41701**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of investments = 2 : 8 : 13

Total profit = 87193

**Formula used:**

Individual share = (Ratio part ÷ Total ratio) × Total profit

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total ratio = 2 + 8 + 13 = 23

⇒ Preeti's share = (2 ÷ 23) × 87193 = 7582

⇒ Reena's share = (13 ÷ 23) × 87193 = 49283

⇒ Difference = 49283 − 7582 = 41701

**∴ The correct answer is 41701.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Partnership Formula

Profit share is proportional to investment ratio: Share = (Individual ratio ÷ Total ratio) × Total profit.

Direct Difference Trick

Difference of shares = Total profit × (Difference of ratios ÷ Total ratio).

Ratio Simplification

Always simplify ratios to reduce calculations and avoid large multiplications.

questions.question: The volume of a rectangular block of wood is 10,368 cm³. Its length, breadth and height are in the ratio of 3 : 2 : 1. If its entire surface is polished at ₹2/cm², then find the total cost of polishing.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let dimensions be 3x, 2x, x

Volume = 3x × 2x × x = 6x³ = 10368

x³ = 1728 ⇒ x = 12

Surface Area = 2(lb + bh + hl) = 2(864 + 288 + 432) = 3168

Cost = 3168 × 2 = 6336

**∴ Answer = 6336**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Volume = 10368 cm³, Ratio = 3 : 2 : 1, Cost = ₹2/cm²

**Formula used:**

Volume = l × b × h, Surface Area = 2(lb + bh + hl)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let l = 3x, b = 2x, h = x

⇒ Volume = 3x × 2x × x = 6x³

⇒ 6x³ = 10368

⇒ x³ = 1728

⇒ x = 12

⇒ l = 36, b = 24, h = 12

⇒ Surface Area = 2(36 × 24 + 24 × 12 + 36 × 12)

⇒ = 2(864 + 288 + 432)

⇒ = 2 × 1584

⇒ = 3168 cm²

⇒ Cost = 3168 × 2 = 6336

**∴ The correct answer is 6336.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cuboid Surface Area

Total Surface Area = 2(lb + bh + hl)

Volume Formula

Volume of cuboid = l × b × h

Ratio Method

Assume dimensions as multiples of x based on ratio to simplify calculations.

questions.question: If the listed price of a bag is 85% more than its cost price and a discount of 49% is announced on it, then find the loss percentage.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Take CP = 100 for quick calculation

MP = 100 + 85 = 185

After 49% discount ⇒ SP = 185 × 51/100

SP = 94.35

Loss = 100 − 94.35 = 5.65%

**∴ Answer = 5.65% loss**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price is 85% more than Cost Price, Discount = 49%

**Formula used:**

SP = MP × (1 − Discount/100), Loss% = (Loss/CP) × 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let CP = 100

⇒ MP = 100 + 85% of 100 = 185

⇒ SP = 185 × (1 − 49/100)

⇒ SP = 185 × 51/100 = 94.35

⇒ Loss = 100 − 94.35 = 5.65

⇒ Loss% = 5.65%

**∴ The correct answer is 5.65% loss.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price Concept

Marked Price = Cost Price + Markup. Here markup = 85% of CP.

Discount Formula

Selling Price = Marked Price × (1 − Discount/100).

Loss Percentage

Loss% = (CP − SP)/CP × 100.

questions.question: The number of prime numbers lying between 415 and 428 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Odd numbers between 415 and 428 not ending in 5 are 417, 419, 421, 423, and 427.

Eliminate multiples of 3 (417, 423) and multiples of 7 (427 = 7 × 61), which leaves 419 and 421.

Both 419 and 421 are not divisible by any prime number up to √428 ≈ 20 (primes 11, 13, 17, 19).

Thus, they are both prime numbers.

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Range of numbers: Between 415 and 428

**Calculations:**

⇒ The numbers between 415 and 428 are: 416, 417, 418, 419, 420, 421, 422, 423, 424, 425, 426, 427.

⇒ Exclude all even numbers and numbers ending with 5, as they are trivially not prime.

⇒ Remaining numbers to check for primality: 417, 419, 421, 423, 427.

⇒ Check divisibility by 3: Sum of digits for 417 (4 + 1 + 7 = 12) and 423 (4 + 2 + 3 = 9) are divisible by 3.

⇒ Remaining possible prime numbers: 419, 421, 427.

⇒ Check divisibility by prime numbers up to √428 ≈ 20 (i.e., check 7, 11, 13, 17, 19).

⇒ For 427: 427 ÷ 7 = 61. Thus, 427 is not a prime number.

⇒ For 419 and 421: Neither number is divisible by 7, 11, 13, 17, or 19.

⇒ Therefore, 419 and 421 are both prime numbers.

⇒ Total prime numbers found = 2.

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Prime Numbers

A natural number greater than 1 that has exactly two distinct positive divisors: 1 and itself.

Checking Primality Rule

To check if a number N is prime, you only need to check its divisibility by all prime numbers less than or equal to √N.

Twin Primes

A pair of prime numbers that differ by exactly 2. For example, 419 and 421 are twin primes.

Co-Primes

Two numbers are co-prime (or mutually prime) if their Highest Common Factor (HCF) is exactly 1.
</p

questions.question: The radius of a ball of iron is 1.5 cm. Three smaller balls are formed by melting it. If the radii of two smaller balls are 0.75 cm and 1.0 cm, find the diameter of the third ball.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Volume conserved ⇒ subtract volumes directly

R³ = r₁³ + r₂³ + r₃³

1.5³ = 0.75³ + 1³ + r₃³

3.375 = 0.421875 + 1 + r₃³

r₃³ = 1.953125 ⇒ r₃ = 1.25

**∴ Diameter = 2.5 cm**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of बड़ा sphere = 1.5 cm

Radii of two small spheres = 0.75 cm, 1 cm

**Formula used:**

Volume of sphere = 4/3 × πr³

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total volume conserved

⇒ 4/3π(1.5)³ = 4/3π[(0.75)³ + 1³ + r₃³]

⇒ (1.5)³ = (0.75)³ + 1 + r₃³

⇒ 3.375 = 0.421875 + 1 + r₃³

⇒ r₃³ = 1.953125

⇒ r₃ = 1.25 cm

⇒ Diameter = 2 × 1.25 = 2.5 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 2.5 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume Conservation

When a solid is melted and reshaped, total volume remains constant.

Sphere Volume Formula

Volume = 4/3 × πr³

Cube Relation Shortcut

In such problems, directly equate r³ values since constants cancel.

questions.question: ₹8,200 is divided among A, B and C in such a way that if ₹19, ₹9 and ₹13 are deducted from their respective shares, they have money in the ratio 12:19:10. Find the difference between B’s and C’s original shares.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Add back deductions to ratio parts

Let adjusted shares = 12x, 19x, 10x

Original shares = 12x+19, 19x+9, 10x+13

Total = 41x + 41 = 8200 ⇒ x = 199

Difference (B − C) = (19x+9) − (10x+13) = 9x − 4 = 1787

**∴ Answer = 1787**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total amount = 8200

After deduction: A : B : C = 12 : 19 : 10

Deductions = 19, 9, 13 respectively

**Formula used:**

Original share = Ratio part × x + deducted value

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let shares after deduction = 12x, 19x, 10x

⇒ Original A = 12x + 19

⇒ Original B = 19x + 9

⇒ Original C = 10x + 13

⇒ Total = (12x+19) + (19x+9) + (10x+13)

⇒ 41x + 41 = 8200

⇒ 41x = 8159

⇒ x = 199

⇒ B = 19x + 9 = 3781 + 9 = 3790

⇒ C = 10x + 13 = 1990 + 13 = 2003

⇒ Difference = 3790 − 2003 = 1787

**∴ The correct answer is 1787.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Adjusted Ratio Concept

When fixed amounts are added or subtracted, convert into algebraic expressions using x.

Linear Equation Formation

Form equation using total sum and solve for unknown multiplier x.

Direct Difference Trick

Difference can be found directly using expression without calculating all shares.

questions.question: Two engines of trains 28 km apart start towards each other at speeds of 23 km/hr and 89 km/hr, respectively. After how much time will they meet each other? (Assume the length of engine is negligible)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the engines are moving towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds.

Relative speed = 23 + 89 = 112 km/hr

Time to meet = Distance ÷ Relative speed = 28 ÷ 112 = 1/4 hours

Time in minutes = 1/4 × 60 = 15 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 15 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
• 
• 
• Total Distance = 28 km 
• 
• 
 23 km/hr Engine 1 
• 
 89 km/hr Engine 2 
• Meeting Point 

**Given:**

Distance between the two engines = 28 km

Speed of the first engine = 23 km/hr

Speed of the second engine = 89 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (opposite directions) = Speed 1 + Speed 2

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative speed = 23 + 89 = 112 km/hr

⇒ Time taken to meet = 28 ÷ 112 hours

⇒ Time = 1/4 hours

⇒ Time in minutes = (1/4) × 60

⇒ Time = 15 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 15 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference between their individual speeds: S = |S₁ − S₂|

Average Speed

When equal distances are covered at speeds a and b consecutively, the average speed for the whole journey is given by 2ab ÷ (a + b).

Passing a Stationary Object

The time taken by a train of length L to pass a point-sized object (like a pole or standing man) is calculated using T = L ÷ Speed of Train.

questions.question: In a quadrilateral QRST, angle Q = 74^circ and angle R = 39^circ . The bisectors of angle S and angle T meet at E. What is the measure of angle TES ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The angle formed by the bisectors of two adjacent angles in a quadrilateral is equal to half the sum of the remaining two angles.

∠TES = (∠Q + ∠R) ÷ 2

⇒ ∠TES = (74° + 39°) ÷ 2

⇒ ∠TES = 113° ÷ 2 = 56.5°

**∴ The correct answer is 56.5°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 

 
• 
 
•

 R (39°)
 S
 T
 E (?)
 
 

 

**Given:**

∠Q = 74°, ∠R = 39°

SE and TE are the angle bisectors of ∠S and ∠T respectively.

**Formula Used:**

Sum of interior angles of a quadrilateral = 360°

Sum of interior angles of a triangle = 180°

**Calculation:**

⇒ ∠Q + ∠R + ∠S + ∠T = 360°

⇒ 74° + 39° + ∠S + ∠T = 360°

⇒ 113° + ∠S + ∠T = 360°

⇒ ∠S + ∠T = 247°

In ΔTES, the sum of internal angles is 180°.

⇒ ∠TES + ∠TSE + ∠STE = 180°

Since SE and TE are the angle bisectors:

⇒ ∠TSE = ∠S ÷ 2

⇒ ∠STE = ∠T ÷ 2

⇒ ∠TES + (∠S ÷ 2) + (∠T ÷ 2) = 180°

⇒ ∠TES + (∠S + ∠T) ÷ 2 = 180°

⇒ ∠TES + (247° ÷ 2) = 180°

⇒ ∠TES + 123.5° = 180°

⇒ ∠TES = 180° − 123.5° = 56.5°

**∴ The correct answer is 56.5°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Interior Angles of a Polygon

The sum of the interior angles of any polygon with n sides is given by the formula: (n − 2) × 180°. For a quadrilateral (n = 4), the sum is always 360°.

Angle Bisector Property in Triangles

If the internal angle bisectors of ∠B and ∠C of a triangle ABC meet at point O, then the angle formed at the center is always given by: ∠BOC = 90° + (∠A ÷ 2).

Cyclic Quadrilateral

If all four vertices of a quadrilateral lie perfectly on the circumference of a circle, it is called a cyclic quadrilateral. The sum of any pair of its opposite angles is exactly 180°.

questions.question: A, B and C together can complete a piece of work in 12 days, while A alone can complete it in 20 days and C alone can complete it in 36 days. In how many days can B alone complete the work?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let Total Work = LCM(12, 20, 36) = 180 units.

Efficiency of (A + B + C) = 180 ÷ 12 = 15 units/day.

Efficiency of A = 180 ÷ 20 = 9 units/day and Efficiency of C = 180 ÷ 36 = 5 units/day.

Efficiency of B = 15 − (9 + 5) = 1 unit/day.

Time taken by B alone = 180 ÷ 1 = 180 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 180 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A, B and C together = 12 days

Time taken by A alone = 20 days

Time taken by C alone = 36 days

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = LCM of Time Taken

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 A + B + C

 180 ÷ 12 = 15

 180 ÷ 20 = 9

 180 ÷ 36 = 5
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of (A + B + C) = 15 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of A = 9 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of C = 5 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of B = Total Efficiency − (Efficiency of A + Efficiency of C)

⇒ Efficiency of B = 15 − (9 + 5) = 15 − 14 = 1 unit/day

⇒ Time taken by B alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of B

⇒ Time taken by B alone = 180 ÷ 1 = 180 days

**∴ The correct answer is 180 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns

Works exactly like Time & Work. An inlet pipe has positive efficiency, while an outlet pipe or leak has negative efficiency. Combined efficiency = Inlet − Outlet.

Work & Wages

Wages are distributed in the ratio of total work done by each individual. If they work for the same number of days, wages are directly distributed in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Alternate Days Work

Find the total work done in a complete cycle (e.g., 2 days). Divide the total work by the cycle work to find the number of full cycles, and then calculate the remaining work sequentially.

questions.question: The sum of two numbers is 54 and their LCM is 195. The two numbers are:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The fastest way to solve this is by verifying the given options.

Option 1: Sum = 32 + 22 = 54, but the LCM of 32 and 22 is 352.

Option 2: Sum = 39 + 15 = 54, and the LCM of 39 and 15 is 195. This satisfies both conditions perfectly.

Option 3: Sum = 44 + 10 = 54, but the LCM of 44 and 10 is 220.

**∴ The correct answer is 39, 15.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sum of two numbers = 54

LCM of two numbers = 195

**Formula Used:**

Let the HCF of the numbers be H. The numbers can be written as Hx and Hy, where x and y are coprime.

Sum = H(x + y)

LCM = H × x × y

 LCM = 195

**Calculations:**

⇒ The HCF (H) must perfectly divide both the sum (54) and the LCM (195).

⇒ Factors of 54: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18, 27, 54

⇒ Factors of 195: 1, 3, 5, 13, 15, 39, 65, 195

⇒ The common factors are 1 and 3. Testing H = 3 for integer values.

⇒ 3(x + y) = 54 ⇒ x + y = 18

⇒ 3 × x × y = 195 ⇒ xy = 65

⇒ We need two coprime numbers that add up to 18 and multiply to 65.

⇒ The numbers 13 and 5 satisfy these conditions (13 + 5 = 18 and 13 × 5 = 65).

⇒ Therefore, x = 13 and y = 5.

⇒ The required numbers are Hx = 3 × 13 = 39 and Hy = 3 × 5 = 15.

**∴ The correct answer is 39, 15.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM and HCF Relationship

For any two numbers A and B, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their HCF and LCM: A × B = HCF × LCM.

Coprime Factors Method

If H is the HCF of two numbers, they can be written as Hx and Hy, where x and y are coprime pairs. Their LCM is strictly given by H × x × y.

HCF Divisibility Rule

The HCF of two given numbers perfectly divides both their sum and their difference.

questions.question: For 15 innings, a cricketer has an average of 94 runs. In the 16th inning, he scores 111 runs. His average score increased by _____. (Round off the answer to the nearest whole number.)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Deviation of the 16th inning score from the old average = 111 − 94 = 17 runs.

This extra 17 runs will be equally distributed among all the 16 innings to find the net increase.

Increase in average = 17 ÷ 16 = 1.0625 runs.

Rounded off to the nearest whole number, the increase is 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 1 run.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average runs for 15 innings = 94

Score in the 16th inning = 111

**Formula Used:**

Average = Sum of observations ÷ Total number of observations

 
 
 

 
 
 
• 
 
 15 Innings (Avg = 94)
 
 
• 
 Extra = +17
 16th Inning
 (Base = 94)
 

 Distribute +17 to all 16 innings
 Net Increase = 17 ÷ 16 ≈ 1

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total runs scored in 15 innings = 15 × 94 = 1410

⇒ Total runs scored in 16 innings = 1410 + 111 = 1521

⇒ New average after 16 innings = 1521 ÷ 16

⇒ New average = 95.0625

⇒ Increase in average score = 95.0625 − 94 = 1.0625

⇒ Rounding off to the nearest whole number, the increase is 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 1 run.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inclusion Method (Net Deviation)

When a new value is added, the change in average is equal to the difference between the new value and the old average, divided by the new total number of observations: Change = (New Value − Old Average) ÷ New Count.

Combined Average

To combine two groups with averages A₁ and A₂ and sizes N₁ and N₂, the combined average is calculated as: (N₁A₁ + N₂A₂) ÷ (N₁ + N₂).

Exclusion Method

When a value is removed, the change in average depends on whether the removed value was higher or lower than the average. If the removed value is higher than the group average, the new average decreases.

questions.question: In an election with two candidates, Candidate A received 75% of the total valid votes. If 10% of the total 14,000 votes were declared invalid, how many valid votes did Candidate B receive?

First remove invalid votes

Valid votes = 90% of 14000 = 12600

B gets remaining after A takes 75%

B = 25% of 12600 = 3150

**∴ Answer = 3150**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total votes = 14000, Invalid = 10%, A gets 75% of valid votes

**Formula used:**

Valid votes = Total × (1 − invalid%)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Invalid votes = 10% of 14000 = 1400

⇒ Valid votes = 14000 − 1400 = 12600

⇒ Votes for A = 75% of 12600 = 9450

⇒ Votes for B = 12600 − 9450 = 3150

**∴ The correct answer is 3150.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Valid Votes Concept

Complementary Percentage

If one candidate gets 75%, the other gets remaining 25%.

Percentage Conversion

Convert percentages into fractions or decimals for quick calculation.

questions.question: {If } 5⁽x ⁻ y⁾ = 125 { and } 5⁽x ⁺ y⁾ = 3125, { find } x.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Express given values as powers of 5: 125 = 5³ and 3125 = 5⁵.

By equating the exponents, we get: x − y = 3 and x + y = 5.

Add the two equations directly: (x − y) + (x + y) = 3 + 5.

⇒ 2x = 8 ⇒ x = 4.

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

5⁽x − y⁾ = 125

5⁽x ⁺ y⁾ = 3125

**Concept Used:**

If am = aⁿ, then m = n.

**Calculations:**

⇒ 125 = 5 × 5 × 5 = 5³

⇒ 3125 = 5 × 5 × 5 × 5 × 5 = 5⁵

⇒ 5⁽x − y⁾ = 5³

⇒ x − y = 3 ---- (1)

⇒ 5⁽x ⁺ y⁾ = 5⁵

⇒ x + y = 5 ---- (2)

⇒ Adding equation (1) and (2):

⇒ (x − y) + (x + y) = 3 + 5

⇒ 2x = 8

⇒ x = 8 ÷ 2

⇒ x = 4

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Product Rule of Exponents

When multiplying terms with the same base, you add their exponents: am × aⁿ = am⁺ⁿ

Quotient Rule of Exponents

When dividing terms with the same base, you subtract their exponents: am ÷ aⁿ = am−ⁿ

Power of a Power Rule

When raising a power to another power, you multiply the exponents: (am)ⁿ = am×ⁿ

Zero Exponent Rule

Any non-zero base raised to the power of zero is equal to one: a⁰ = 1

questions.question: The expenditure of Sudha is 150% more than her savings. If her expenditure decreases by 3% and savings increase by 21.5%, then by what percentage does her income increase?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let savings = 100 ⇒ expenditure = 250 (since 150% more)

Income = 350

New expenditure = 250 × 97/100 = 242.5

New savings = 100 × 121.5/100 = 121.5

New income = 242.5 + 121.5 = 364

Increase = 364 − 350 = 14 ⇒ % increase = 14/350 × 100 = 4%

**∴ Answer = 4%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Expenditure is 150% more than savings

Expenditure decreases by 3%, Savings increase by 21.5%

Income = Expenditure + Savings

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let savings = 100

⇒ Expenditure = 100 + 150% of 100 = 250

⇒ Original income = 250 + 100 = 350

⇒ New expenditure = 250 × (1 − 3/100) = 242.5

⇒ New savings = 100 × (1 + 21.5/100) = 121.5

⇒ New income = 242.5 + 121.5 = 364

⇒ Increase = 364 − 350 = 14

⇒ % increase = (14 ÷ 350) × 100 = 4%

**∴ The correct answer is 4%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income Relation

Income = Savings + Expenditure always holds true.

Percentage Change Formula

New value = Original × (1 ± percentage/100).

Assumption Method

questions.question: Three chairs and two tables together cost ₹600, two chairs and one table together cost ₹350. The cost of four chairs is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Equate the number of tables to find the cost of a chair directly.

2 × (2 chairs + 1 table) = 2 × 350 = 700

Subtract the first condition from this result:

(4 chairs + 2 tables) − (3 chairs + 2 tables) = 700 − 600

1 chair = 100 ⇒ 4 chairs = 400

**∴ The correct answer is ₹400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost of 3 chairs and 2 tables = ₹600

Cost of 2 chairs and 1 table = ₹350

**Calculation:**

Let the cost of one chair be C and one table be T.

⇒ 3C + 2T = 600 ... (i)

⇒ 2C + T = 350 ... (ii)

Multiply equation (ii) by 2 to make the coefficient of T equal:

⇒ 4C + 2T = 700 ... (iii)

Subtract equation (i) from equation (iii):

⇒ (4C + 2T) − (3C + 2T) = 700 − 600

⇒ C = 100

The cost of 1 chair is ₹100.

Now, calculate the cost of 4 chairs:

⇒ 4 × 100 = 400

**∴ The correct answer is ₹400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Linear Equations in Two Variables

An equation of the form ax + by + c = 0 where a, b, and c are real numbers is a linear equation. They can be solved easily using substitution, elimination, or cross-multiplication methods.

Elimination Method

Multiply one or both equations by suitable constants to make the coefficients of one variable equal, then add or subtract to eliminate that variable. This is often the fastest method for pricing and quantity problems.

Substitution Method

Express one variable in terms of the other from one equation and substitute this expression into the other equation to find the value of the second variable.
